homonyms.basis: The census row carries no disambiguation field. No card is a homonym: cards 1 and 3 are the Lab's partners' pages, cards 2 and 4 the Lab's own site. The address names the database; the composition gives the Lab first, which the census keeps apart (LS-40, 'NOT the Creative AI Lab as a whole'), and reaches the database by name (per_dim reached 'same'). 'Creative AI Database' (the Notion page's address) and 'creative-ai.org' are names of the entity (census aka).
distinct_entities: the Creative AI Lab, the research programme and partnership that produces the database (B1, B2, B3; LS-40)
the launch list of 65 essential tools contributed by Luba Elliott (B7 F47), a contribution to the database at launch
HOLO, the editorial and curatorial platform that reported the launch (B7 F48)
Serpentine Galleries and its Arts Technologies and R&D Platform; King's College London's Department of Digital Humanities (the partners)
Future Art Ecosystems, Serpentine's report series beside the Lab (B2 F22)
the tools and resources the database lists (Sora, Mustango and the rest), each its makers' own

captures.description: THE DATABASE, SIGNED OUT, 2026-11-01: 'The Creative AI Lab is a joint research partnership between Serpentine Arts Technologies and the Department of Digital Humanities at King's College London.' Key overview (launch date; partners and funders, among them 'Google's Artists + Machine Intelligence Grant'; core mission); the database (purpose; evaluation criteria 'transparency, creative malleability, technical interoperability, research caliber, and public value'; four categories of tools, Audio to Detection / Tracking). Four cards: Serpentine, Creative AI Lab (two), King's College London.
